deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page has three layers: (A) brown-ink formulas at the top on the kinematics of a homogeneous liquid ellipsoid, i.e. the Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann problem; (B) a pencil draft of a formal letter or expert opinion (Gutachten); (C) pencil algebra written upside down in the lower half.

(A) KINEMATICS OF THE LIQUID ELLIPSOID.
Riemann writes a 3x3 array of time derivatives:
- dl/dt, dm/dt, dn/dt
- dl'/dt, dm'/dt, dn'/dt
- dl''/dt, dm''/dt, dn''/dt

These are derivatives of the coefficients of the linear map x = M xi, which sends the particles of a reference sphere (or ellipsoid) to their present positions. Rows are (l,m,n), (l',m',n'), (l'',m'',n''). In Dedekind's and Riemann's 1860–61 treatment M = R1 · diag(a,b,c) · R2^T, with R1 and R2 rotations.

Top left he notes that at the instant considered the axes coincide, so l = a, m' = b, n'' = c and M is diagonal. [My reading of the faint note.]

Then dM/dt = Ω1·D − D·Ω2 + dD/dt, where Ω1 and Ω2 are the antisymmetric angular-velocity matrices of the two rotations. Write the (2,3)-rotation components as p for R1 and p' for R2. Then:
- dn'/dt = dM23/dt = b p' − c p
- dm''/dt = dM32/dt = b p − c p'

Adding and subtracting gives the two lines in the top right:
- dm''/dt + dn'/dt = (b−c)(p+p') = 2u(b−c), with u = (p+p')/2
- dm''/dt − dn'/dt = (b+c)(p−p') = 2u'(b+c), with u' = (p−p')/2

These are exactly Riemann's variables of the 1861 paper. The symmetric and antisymmetric parts of the off-diagonal velocity gradient are controlled by (b−c)u and (b+c)u'.

Special cases noted on the page:
- b = c gives dm''/dt = −dn'/dt (top left), and db/dt = dc/dt if the symmetry is to persist.
- a = b = c gives dm''/dt + dn'/dt = 0.

The middle line, partly struck, has the form (b−a)(b+a)(dl'/dt + dm/dt)… It is the analogous (1,2)-plane combination: dl'/dt + dm/dt = (a−b)(r+r') and dl'/dt − dm/dt = (a+b)(r−r'). Multiplying sum and difference eliminates a+b and a−b separately: (dl'/dt)^2 − (dm/dt)^2 = (a^2−b^2)(r^2−r'^2). This is evidently the beginning of eliminating the angular variables. The completion is mine; the fragment breaks off.

(B) LETTER DRAFT (pencil, heavily corrected).
- Salutation: 'Hochgeborner Herr Graf / Hochzuverehrender Herr Geheimer Rath!' These are probably two alternative addresses.
- Struck opening: 'Ew. Hochgeboren haben in Ihrem geschätzten Schreiben …'.
- Main text (my best reading): 'Der gehorsamst Unterzeichnete bedauert, daß durch eine heftige Erkältung [?], welche ihn zeitweilig an das Bett gefesselt hat, die Beantwortung [?] verzögert worden ist, und Ew. Hochwohlgeboren …'.
- Then: 'So habe ich nun auch versucht, um …'.
- Separate passage near the top: 'Die Ausführung dieses Unternehmens würde einen wichtigen Beitrag zu unserer Kenntniß der Gestalt der Erde … Sie würde auch für die Vervollkommnung der Methoden der Rechnung wichtig werden …'.

So this is an opinion on a geodetic enterprise concerning the figure of the Earth. It is most plausibly Baeyer's Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (1861/62), on which German governments solicited expert advice. Riemann's illness (pleurisy, 1862) fits the excuse. This identification is my conjecture.

The ellipsoid kinematics fits the same period (Riemann's paper was presented in 1860/61). Thematically the Earth's figure and rotating fluid ellipsoids are linked.

(C) UPSIDE-DOWN ALGEBRA.
The pieces include:
- (3(1+x) − 8x)^2
- −12x·3(1+x) + 12·16x^2
- 12x((1+x)^2 − 4x)
- 3(1+x) − 2x
- 3 − 4x + 3x^2 (reading uncertain)
- fractions in b^2+c^2, b^2−c^2, b^2c^2 such as 2(b^2+c^2)/(b^2−c^2)^2 and 3/ε^2 − 3·…
- a final relation of the form 3·…/(…) = 1/6 + x/6.

This looks like reducing a symmetric expression in b^2, c^2 to one variable x (probably a ratio such as b^2/c^2, or a squared eccentricity). It may be a discriminant-type expression in x, conceivably for equilibrium or stability conditions of the ellipsoid. The fragments are too incomplete and too uncertain in reading to reconstruct a coherent derivation; I do not claim one.
errors: No mathematical error in the two main identities. With M = diag(a,b,c) at the instant and dM/dt = Ω1 D − D Ω2, one gets dm''/dt + dn'/dt = (b−c)(p+p') and dm''/dt − dn'/dt = (b+c)(p−p') exactly. Riemann's sign conventions for p, p' may differ from mine by an overall sign; this is immaterial.
The (1,2)-plane line (b−a)(b+a)(…) is incomplete and partly struck, so it cannot be checked as written.

The upside-down algebra is too fragmentary to verify. As read, (3(1+x)−8x)^2 = (3−5x)^2 does not visibly reduce to the nearby '3−4x+3x^2', so either the reading is wrong or these are separate intermediate expressions.

results.what: Decomposition of the off-diagonal time derivatives of the deformation matrix of a homogeneous liquid ellipsoid. dm''/dt + dn'/dt = (b−c)(p+p') = 2u(b−c) and dm''/dt − dn'/dt = (b+c)(p−p') = 2u'(b+c), with special cases b=c and a=b=c.
results.modern_name: Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann kinematics of self-gravitating fluid ellipsoids: Riemann ellipsoids, decomposition into figure rotation and internal vorticity
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1857/60, posthumous), Dedekind (1860), Riemann (1861, 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides')

results.what: Elimination step multiplying the sum and difference of the (1,2) off-diagonal derivatives to get the product (a^2−b^2)(r^2−r'^2)
results.modern_name: Elementary elimination in the Riemann ellipsoid equations

results.what: Draft of an expert opinion or letter on a geodetic enterprise concerning the figure of the Earth, probably the Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung, with apology for a delay due to illness
results.modern_name: Historical/biographical document (Riemann's involvement in geodetic advisory matters)

results.what: Algebraic reduction of expressions in b^2, c^2 to a single variable x
results.modern_name: Unidentified elementary algebra, possibly a discriminant or stability condition

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the kinematic set-up of Riemann's own published 1861 paper on liquid ellipsoids, written in his notation (u, u' as half-sums and half-differences of the rotation rates). It is a working draft of known Riemann material. The letter draft hints at a geodetic consultation (figure of the Earth) and an illness, which is of minor biographical interest. It is not mathematically surprising.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,p,pp=symbols('a b c p pp'); D=diag(a,b,c); W1=Matrix([[0,0,0],[0,0,-p],[0,p,0]]); W2=Matrix([[0,0,0],[0,0,-pp],[0,pp,0]]); Md=W1*D-D*W2; simplify(Md[2,1]+Md[1,2]-(b-c)*(p+pp))
checkable.asserts: dm''/dt + dn'/dt = (b-c)(p+p') at the instant M = diag(a,b,c); m'' = M[2,1], n' = M[1,2]. Should simplify to 0.
For b=c the sum vanishes, i.e. dm''/dt = -dn'/dt. Result 0.
(1,2)-plane analogue with l' = M[1,0], m = M[0,1]: (dl'/dt)^2 - (dm/dt)^2 = (a^2-b^2)(r^2-r'^2). Result 0.
dl'/dt + dm/dt = (a-b)(r+r') and dl'/dt - dm/dt = (a+b)(r-r'). Both give 0.
Expands the upside-down fragment: gives 25*x**2 - 30*x + 9, i.e. (3-5x)^2.

transcription_corrections: Top right: '(b−c) p p'' should read '(b−c)(p+p')'.
Top right: '= 2n(b−c)' should read '= 2u(b−c)', and '= 2n'(b+c)' should read '= 2u'(b+c)'. The letters are u, u' (Riemann's notation), not n, n'.
Top left first line reads approximately 'l=a m'=b n''=c': the diagonal entries equal the semi-axes at the instant considered.
'Das geschätzte Unternehmen bedauert' is more likely 'Der gehorsamst Unterzeichnete bedauert, daß durch eine heftige Erkältung [?] …'.
'welches ihr zeitweilig in das Bett …' is more likely 'welche ihn zeitweilig an das Bett gefesselt …'.
'eine wichtige Beitrag für unsere Kenntniß' is better read as 'einen wichtigen Beitrag zu unserer Kenntniß der Gestalt der Erde'.
The lower-half formulas are written upside down. Several readings ('3−4x+3x^2', '1/6 + x/6') are uncertain, and many fractions in b^2±c^2 are omitted from the machine transcription.
